text: Considering only the principal values of inverse trigonometric functions, the number of positive real values of $x$ satisfying $\tan ^{-1}(x)+\tan ^{-1}(2x)=\frac{π}{4}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \tan ^{-1}x+\tan ^{-1}2x=\dfrac{π}{4};x>0 \\ \Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}2x=\dfrac{π}{4}-\tan ^{-1}x \end{array}$

Taking tan both sides

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 2\mathrm{x}=\dfrac{1-\mathrm{x}}{1+\mathrm{x}} \\ \Rightarrow 2\mathrm{x}^{2}+3\mathrm{x}-1=0 \\ \mathrm{x}=\dfrac{-3\pm \sqrt{9+8}}{4}=\dfrac{-3\pm \sqrt{17}}{4} \end{array}$

Only possible $x=\frac{-3+\sqrt{17}}{4}$

text: Let the image of the point $(1,0,7)$ in the line $\frac{x}{1}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z-2}{3}$ be the point $(α,β,γ)$. Then which one of the following points lies on the line passing through $(α,β,γ)$ and making angles $\frac{2π}{3}$ and $\frac{3π}{4}$ with $y$-axis and $z$-axis respectively and an acute angle with $x$-axis ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{L}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{x}}{1}=\frac{\mathrm{y}-1}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-2}{3}=λ$


[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{M}(λ,1+2λ,2+3λ) \\ \mathrm{PM}\leftarrow =(λ-1)\hat{\mathrm{i}}+(1+2λ)\hat{\mathrm{j}}+(3λ-5)\hat{\mathrm{k}} \end{array}$

$\mathrm{PM}\leftarrow$ is perpendicular to line $\mathrm{L}_{1}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{PM}\leftarrow \vec{\mathrm{b}}=0(\vec{\mathrm{b}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2\hat{\mathrm{j}}+3\hat{\mathrm{k}}) \\ \Rightarrow λ-1+4λ+2+9λ-15=0 \\ 14λ=14\Rightarrow λ=1 \\ \therefore \mathrm{M}=(1,3,5) \\ \vec{\mathrm{Q}}=2\vec{\mathrm{M}}-\vec{\mathrm{P}}[\mathrm{M}\text{is midpoint of}\vec{\mathrm{P}}&\vec{\mathrm{Q}}] \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \vec{\mathrm{Q}}=2\hat{\mathrm{i}}+6\hat{\mathrm{j}}+10\hat{\mathrm{k}}-\hat{\mathrm{i}}-7\hat{\mathrm{k}} \\ \vec{\mathrm{Q}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+6\hat{\mathrm{j}}+3\hat{\mathrm{k}} \\ \therefore (α,β,γ)=(1,6,3) \end{array}$

Required line having direction cosine $(l,\mathrm{m},\mathrm{n})$

$\begin{array}{l} l^{2}+m^{2}+n^{2}=1 \\ \Rightarrow l^{2}+\left (-\dfrac{1}{2}\right )^{2}+\left (-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )^{2}=1 \end{array}$

$l^{2}=\frac{1}{4}$

$\therefore l=\frac{1}{2}$ [Line make acute angle with $\mathrm{x}$-axis]

Equation of line passing through $(1,6,3)$ will be

$\vec{\mathrm{r}}=(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+6\hat{\mathrm{j}}+3\hat{\mathrm{k}})+μ\left (\frac{1}{2}\hat{\mathrm{i}}-\frac{1}{2}\hat{\mathrm{j}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{\mathrm{k}}\right )$

Option (3) satisfying for $μ=4$

text: Let $A$ and $B$ be two finite sets with $m$ and $n$ elements respectively. The total number of subsets of the set $A$ is 56 more than the total number of subsets of $B$. Then the distance of the point $P(m,n)$ from the point $Q(-2,-3)$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} 2^{\mathrm{m}}-2^{\mathrm{n}}=56 \\ 2^{\mathrm{n}}\left (2^{\mathrm{m}-\mathrm{n}}-1\right )=2^{3}\times 7 \\ 2^{\mathrm{n}}=2^{3}\text{and}2^{\mathrm{m}-\mathrm{n}}-1=7 \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=3\text{and}2^{\mathrm{m}-\mathrm{n}}=8 \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=3\text{and}\mathrm{m}-\mathrm{n}=3 \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=3\text{and}\mathrm{m}=6 \\ \mathrm{P}(6,3)\text{and}\mathrm{Q}(-2,-3) \\ \mathrm{PQ}=\sqrt{8^{2}+6^{2}}=\sqrt{100}=10 \end{array}$

Hence option (2) is correct

text: Let $f:𝐑-\left \{\frac{-1}{2}\right \}\to 𝐑$ and $g:𝐑-\left \{\frac{-5}{2}\right \}\to 𝐑$ be defined as $f(x)=\frac{2x+3}{2x+1}$ and $g(x)=\frac{|x|+1}{2x+5}$. Then, the domain of the function fog is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$g$ is defined for $x\neq -\dfrac{5}{2}$, and $f(g(x))$ is defined when, in addition, $g(x)\neq -\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Setting $g(x)=-\dfrac{1}{2}$:

$\dfrac{|x|+1}{2x+5}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\Rightarrow 2|x|+2=-2x-5\Rightarrow 2|x|+2x=-7$

For $x\geq 0$ this gives $4x=-7$, which has no solution with $x\geq 0$; for $x<0$, $|x|=-x$ gives $0=-7$, which is impossible.

So $g(x)\neq -\dfrac{1}{2}$ for every $x\neq -\dfrac{5}{2}$. The value $x=-\dfrac{7}{4}$ arises only if $|x|$ is replaced by $x$; in fact $g\left (-\dfrac{7}{4}\right )=\dfrac{11/4}{3/2}=\dfrac{11}{6}$.

Therefore the domain of $f\circ g$ is $𝐑-\left \{-\dfrac{5}{2}\right \}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift

text: $\text{If}\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{3+α\sin x+β\cos x+\log _{e}(1-x)}{3\tan ^{2}x}=\frac{1}{3}\text{, then}2α-β\text{is equal to :}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{3+α\sin x+β\cos x+\log _{e}(1-x)}{3\tan ^{2}x}=\frac{1}{3}$

$\Rightarrow \lim _{x\to 0}\frac{3+α\left [x-\frac{x3}{3!}+\ldots .\right ]+β\left [1-\frac{x2}{2!}+\frac{x4}{4!}\ldots .\right ]+\left (-x-\frac{x2}{2}-\frac{x3}{3}\ldots \right )}{3\tan ^{2}x}=\frac{1}{3}$

$\Rightarrow \lim _{x\to 0}\frac{(3+β)+(α-1)x+\left (-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{β}{2}\right )x^{2}+\ldots .}{3x^{2}}\times \frac{x^{2}}{\tan ^{2}x}=\frac{1}{3}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow β+3=0,α-1=0\text{and}\dfrac{-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{β}{2}}{3}=\dfrac{1}{3} \\ \Rightarrow β=-3,α=1 \\ \Rightarrow 2α-β=2+3=5 \end{array}$

text: If $y=y(x)$ is the solution curve of the differential equation $\left (x^{2}-4\right )\mathrm{d}y-\left (y^{2}-3y\right )\mathrm{d}x=0,x>2,y(4)=\frac{3}{2}$ and the slope of the curve is never zero, then the value of $y(10)$ equals :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \left (x^{2}-4\right )dy-\left (y^{2}-3y\right )dx=0 \\ \Rightarrow \int \dfrac{dy}{y^{2}-3y}=\int \dfrac{dx}{x^{2}-4} \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{3}\int \dfrac{y-(y-3)}{y(y-3)}dy=\int \dfrac{dx}{x^{2}-4} \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{3}(\ln |y-3|-\ln |y|)=\dfrac{1}{4}\ln \left |\dfrac{x-2}{x+2}\right |+C \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{3}\ln \left |\dfrac{y-3}{y}\right |=\dfrac{1}{4}\ln \left |\dfrac{x-2}{x+2}\right |+C \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{At}\mathrm{x}=4,\mathrm{y}=\dfrac{3}{2} \\ \therefore \mathrm{C}=\dfrac{1}{4}\ln 3 \\ \therefore \dfrac{1}{3}\ln \left |\dfrac{\mathrm{y}-3}{\mathrm{y}}\right |=\dfrac{1}{4}\ln \left |\dfrac{\mathrm{x}-2}{\mathrm{x}+2}\right |+\dfrac{1}{4}\ln (3) \\ \text{At}\mathrm{x}=10 \\ \dfrac{1}{3}\ln \left |\dfrac{\mathrm{y}-3}{\mathrm{y}}\right |=\dfrac{1}{4}\ln \left |\dfrac{2}{3}\right |+\dfrac{1}{4}\ln (3) \\ \ln \left |\dfrac{\mathrm{y}-3}{\mathrm{y}}\right |=\ln 2^{3/4},\forall \mathrm{x}>2,\dfrac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}<0 \\ \text{as}\mathrm{y}(4)=\dfrac{3}{2}\Rightarrow \mathrm{y}\in (0,3) \\ -\mathrm{y}+3=8^{1/4}\cdot \mathrm{y} \\ \mathrm{y}=\dfrac{3}{1+8^{1/4}} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift

text: If $2\tan ^{2}θ-5\sec θ=1$ has exactly 7 solutions in the interval $\left [0,\frac{nπ}{2}\right ]$, for the least value of $n\in 𝐍$, then $\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\frac{k}{2^{k}}$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} 2\tan ^{2}θ-5\sec θ-1=0 \\ \Rightarrow 2\sec ^{2}θ-5\sec θ-3=0 \\ \Rightarrow (2\sec θ+1)(\sec θ-3)=0 \\ \Rightarrow \sec θ=-\dfrac{1}{2},3 \\ \Rightarrow \cos θ=-2,\dfrac{1}{3} \\ \Rightarrow \cos θ=\dfrac{1}{3} \end{array}$

For 7 solutions $\mathrm{n}=13$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{So,}\sum\limits _{\mathrm{k}=1}^{13}\dfrac{\mathrm{k}}{2^{\mathrm{k}}}=\mathrm{S}\text{(say)} \\ \mathrm{S}=\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{2}{2^{2}}+\dfrac{3}{2^{3}}+\ldots .+\dfrac{13}{2^{13}} \\ \dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{S}=\dfrac{1}{2^{2}}+\dfrac{1}{2^{3}}+\ldots .+\dfrac{12}{2^{13}}+\dfrac{13}{2^{14}} \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{\mathrm{S}}{2}=\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot \dfrac{1-\frac{1}{2^{13}}}{1-\frac{1}{2}}-\dfrac{13}{2^{14}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{S}=2\cdot \left (\dfrac{2^{13}-1}{2^{13}}\right )-\dfrac{13}{2^{13}} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift

text: Let $g(x)=3f\left (\frac{x}{3}\right )+f(3-x)$ and $f^{''}(x)>0$ for all $x\in (0,3)$. If $g$ is decreasing in $(0,α)$ and increasing in $(α,3)$, then $8α$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$g(x)=3f\left (\frac{x}{3}\right )+f(3-x)\text{and}f^{''}(x)>0\forall x\in (0,3)$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}^{'}(\mathrm{x})$ is increasing function

$\begin{array}{l} g^{'}(x)=3\times \dfrac{1}{3}\cdot f^{'}\left (\dfrac{x}{3}\right )-f^{'}(3-x) \\ =f^{'}\left (\dfrac{x}{3}\right )-f^{'}(3-x) \end{array}$

If $\mathrm{g}$ is decreasing in $(0,α)$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{g}^{'}(\mathrm{x})<0 \\ \mathrm{f}^{'}\left (\dfrac{\mathrm{x}}{3}\right )-\mathrm{f}^{'}(3-\mathrm{x})<0 \\ \mathrm{f}^{'}\left (\dfrac{\mathrm{x}}{3}\right )<\mathrm{f}^{'}(3-\mathrm{x}) \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{\mathrm{x}}{3}<3-\mathrm{x} \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}<\dfrac{9}{4} \end{array}$

Therefore $α=\frac{9}{4}$

Then $8α=8\times \frac{9}{4}=18$

text: Let $\mathrm{R}$ be the interior region between the lines $3x-y+1=0$ and $x+2y-5=0$ containing the origin. The set of all values of $a$, for which the points $\left (a^{2},a+1\right )$ lie in $R$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Let $L_{1}(x,y)=3x-y+1$ and $L_{2}(x,y)=x+2y-5$. The point $P\left (a^{2},a+1\right )$ lies in $R$ exactly when it is on the same side of each line as the origin $O$.


[IMG]

$L_{1}(O)=1>0$, so $L_{1}(P)$ must be positive:

$3a^{2}-(a+1)+1=a(3a-1)>0\Rightarrow a\in (-\infty ,0)\cup \left (\dfrac{1}{3},\infty \right )$

$L_{2}(O)=-5<0$, so $L_{2}(P)$ must be negative:

$a^{2}+2(a+1)-5=a^{2}+2a-3=(a+3)(a-1)<0\Rightarrow a\in (-3,1)$

Both conditions together give

$a\in (-3,0)\cup \left (\dfrac{1}{3},1\right )$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift

solution.body:
$α=\dfrac{(4!)!}{(4!)^{3!}}=\dfrac{24!}{(4!)^{6}}$ and $β=\dfrac{(5!)!}{(5!)^{4!}}=\dfrac{120!}{(5!)^{24}}$.

The number of ways to put 24 distinct objects into 6 distinct boxes with 4 objects in each box is ${}^{24}C_{4}\times {}^{20}C_{4}\times \cdots \times {}^{4}C_{4}=\dfrac{24!}{(4!)^{6}}$. Being a count, it is a natural number, so $α\in 𝐍$.

In the same way, $\dfrac{120!}{(5!)^{24}}$ is the number of ways to put 120 distinct objects into 24 distinct boxes with 5 objects in each box, so $β\in 𝐍$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: The integral $\int \frac{\left (x^{8}-x^{2}\right )\mathrm{d}x}{(x^{12}+3x^{6}+1)\tan ^{-1}\left (x^{3}+\frac{1}{x3}\right )}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I=\int \frac{x^{8}-x^{2}}{(x^{12}+3x^{6}+1)\tan ^{-1}\left (x^{3}+\frac{1}{x3}\right )}dx$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Let}\tan ^{-1}\left (x^{3}+\dfrac{1}{x^{3}}\right )=t \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{1+\left (x^{3}+\frac{1}{x^{3}}\right )^{2}}\cdot \left (3x^{2}-\dfrac{3}{x^{4}}\right )dx=dt \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{x^{6}}{x^{12}+3x^{6}+1}\cdot \dfrac{3x^{6}-3}{x^{4}}dx=dt \\ I=\dfrac{1}{3}\int \dfrac{dt}{t}=\dfrac{1}{3}\ln |t|+C \\ I=\dfrac{1}{3}\ln \left |\tan ^{-1}\left (x^{3}+\dfrac{1}{x^{3}}\right )\right |+C \\ I=\ln \left |\tan ^{-1}\left (x^{3}+\dfrac{1}{x^{3}}\right )\right |^{1/3}+C \end{array}$

Hence option (1) is correct.

text: For $0<\mathrm{a}<1$, the value of the integral $\int\limits _{0}^{π}\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{1-2\mathrm{a}\cos x+\mathrm{a}^{2}}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Replacing $x$ by $π-x$ gives $I=\int\limits _{0}^{π}\dfrac{dx}{1+2a\cos x+a^{2}}$. Adding the two forms:

$2I=\int\limits _{0}^{π}\dfrac{2(1+a^{2})}{(1+a^{2})^{2}-4a^{2}\cos ^{2}x}dx=2\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\dfrac{2(1+a^{2})}{(1+a^{2})^{2}-4a^{2}\cos ^{2}x}dx$

since this integrand is unchanged by $x\to π-x$.

Dividing numerator and denominator by $\cos ^{2}x$ and using $\sec ^{2}x=1+\tan ^{2}x$:

$I=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\dfrac{2(1+a^{2})\sec ^{2}x}{(1+a^{2})^{2}\tan ^{2}x+(1-a^{2})^{2}}dx$

Put $\tan x=u$ (limits $0$ to $\infty$) and $c=\dfrac{1-a^{2}}{1+a^{2}}>0$ for $0<a<1$:

$I=\dfrac{2}{1+a^{2}}\int\limits _{0}^{\infty }\dfrac{du}{u^{2}+c^{2}}=\dfrac{2}{1+a^{2}}\cdot \dfrac{1}{c}\cdot \dfrac{π}{2}=\dfrac{π}{1-a^{2}}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift

text: The mean and standard deviation of 15 observations were found to be 12 and 3 respectively. On rechecking it was found that an observation was read as 10 in place of 12 . If $μ$ and $σ^{2}$ denote the mean and variance of the correct observations respectively, then $15\left (μ+μ^{2}+σ^{2}\right )$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the incorrect mean be $μ^{'}$ and standard deviation be $σ^{'}$

We have

$μ^{'}=\frac{\Sigma \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}}{15}=12\Rightarrow \Sigma \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}=180$

As per given information correct $\Sigma \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}=180-10+12$

$\Rightarrow μ(\text{correct mean})=\frac{182}{15}$

Also

$σ^{'}=\sqrt{\frac{\Sigma \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}^{2}}{15}-144}=3\Rightarrow \Sigma \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}^{2}=2295$

Correct $\Sigma \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}{}^{2}=2295-100+144=2339$

$σ^{2}(\text{correct variance})=\frac{2339}{15}-\frac{182\times 182}{15\times 15}$

Required value

$\begin{array}{l} =15\left (μ+μ^{2}+σ^{2}\right ) \\ =15\left (\dfrac{182}{15}+\dfrac{182\times 182}{15\times 15}+\dfrac{2339}{15}-\dfrac{182\times 182}{15\times 15}\right ) \\ =15\left (\dfrac{182}{15}+\dfrac{2339}{15}\right ) \\ =2521 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift

text: The coefficient of $x^{2012}$ in the expansion of $(1-x)^{2008}\left (1+x+x^{2}\right )^{2007}$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} (1-x)(1-x)^{2007}\left (1+x+x^{2}\right )^{2007} \\ (1-x)\left (1-x^{3}\right )^{2007} \\ (1-x)\left ({}^{2007}C_{0}-{}^{2007}C_{1}\left (x^{3}\right )+\ldots \ldots .\right ) \end{array}$

General term

$\begin{array}{l} (1-x)\left ((-1)^{r}{}^{2007}C_{r}x^{3r}\right ) \\ (-1)^{r2007}C_{r}x^{3r}-(-1)^{r2007}C_{r}x^{3r+1} \\ 3r=2012 \\ r\neq \dfrac{2012}{3} \\ 3r+1=2012 \\ 3r=2011 \\ r\neq \dfrac{2011}{3} \end{array}$

Hence there is no term containing $\mathrm{x}^{2012}$.

So coefficient of $\mathrm{x}^{2012}=0$

text: The lines $\frac{x-2}{2}=\frac{y}{-2}=\frac{z-7}{16}$ and $\frac{x+3}{4}=\frac{y+2}{3}=\frac{z+2}{1}$ intersect at the point $P$. If the distance of $\mathrm{P}$ from the line $\frac{x+1}{2}=\frac{y-1}{3}=\frac{z-1}{1}$ is $l$, then $14l^{2}$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{\mathrm{x}-2}{1}=\dfrac{\mathrm{y}}{-1}=\dfrac{\mathrm{z}-7}{8}=λ \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{x}+3}{4}=\dfrac{\mathrm{y}+2}{3}=\dfrac{\mathrm{z}+2}{1}=\mathrm{k} \\ \Rightarrow λ+2=4\mathrm{k}-3 \\ -λ=3\mathrm{k}-2 \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=1,λ=-1 \\ 8λ+7=\mathrm{k}-2 \\ \therefore \mathrm{P}=(1,1,-1) \end{array}$


[IMG]


Projection of $2\hat{i}-2\hat{k}$ on $2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ is

$\begin{array}{l} =\dfrac{4-2}{\sqrt{4+9+1}}=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{14}} \\ \therefore l^{2}=8-\dfrac{4}{14}=\dfrac{108}{14} \\ \Rightarrow 14l^{2}=108 \end{array}$

text:
Let $f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{x}g(t)\log _{\mathrm{e}}\left (\frac{1-\mathrm{t}}{1+\mathrm{t}}\right )\mathrm{dt}$, where $g$ is a continuous odd function.
If $\int\limits _{-π/2}^{π/2}\left (f(x)+\frac{x^{2}\cos x}{1+\mathrm{e}^{x}}\right )\mathrm{d}x=\left (\frac{π}{α}\right )^{2}-α$, then $α$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{x}g(t)\ln \left (\frac{1-t}{1+t}\right )dt$

$f(-x)=\int\limits _{0}^{-x}g(t)\ln \left (\frac{1-t}{1+t}\right )dt$

$f(-x)=-\int\limits _{0}^{x}g(-y)\ln \left (\frac{1+y}{1-y}\right )dy$

$=-\int\limits _{0}^{x}g(y)\ln \left (\frac{1-y}{1+y}\right )dy$ (g is odd)

$f(-x)=-f(x)\Rightarrow f$ is also odd

Now,

$\begin{array}{l} I=\int\limits _{-π/2}^{π/2}\left (f(x)+\dfrac{x^{2}\cos x}{1+e^{x}}\right )dx\text{... (1)} \\ I=\int\limits _{-π/2}^{π/2}\left (f(-x)+\dfrac{x^{2}e^{x}\cos x}{1+e^{x}}\right )dx\text{... (2)} \\ 2I=\int\limits _{-π/2}^{π/2}x^{2}\cos xdx=2\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}x^{2}\cos xdx \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} I=\left (x^{2}\sin x\right )_{0}^{π/2}-\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}2x\sin xdx \\ =\dfrac{π^{2}}{4}-2\left (-x\cos x+\int \cos xdx\right )_{0}^{π/2} \\ =\dfrac{π^{2}}{4}-2(0+1)=\dfrac{π^{2}}{4}-2\Rightarrow \left (\dfrac{π}{2}\right )^{2}-2 \\ \therefore α=2 \end{array}$

text: If the sum of squares of all real values of $α$, for which the lines $2x-y+3=0,6x+3y+1=0$ and $αx+2y-2=0$ do not form a triangle is $p$, then the greatest integer less than or equal to $p$ is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} 2x-y+3=0 \\ 6x+3y+1=0 \\ αx+2y-2=0 \end{array}$

Will not form a $\Delta$ if $αx+2y-2=0$ is concurrent with $2x-y+3=0$ and $6x+3y+1=0$ or parallel to either of them so

Case-1: Concurrent lines

$\left |\begin{array}{lll} 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 6 & 3 & 1 \\ α & 2 & -2 \end{array}\right |=0\Rightarrow α=\frac{4}{5}$

Case-2 : Parallel lines

$\begin{array}{l} -\dfrac{α}{2}=\dfrac{-6}{3}\text{or}-\dfrac{α}{2}=2 \\ \Rightarrow α=4\text{or}α=-4 \\ P=16+16+\dfrac{16}{25} \\ [P]=\left [32+\dfrac{16}{25}\right ]=32 \end{array}$

text: Let $A$ be a $2\times 2$ real matrix and $I$ be the identity matrix of order 2. If the roots of the equation $|\mathrm{A}-x\mathrm{I}|=0$ be $-1$ and 3, then the sum of the diagonal elements of the matrix $\mathrm{A}^{2}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$|A-xI|=0$

Roots are $-$1 and 3

Sum of roots $=\mathrm{tr}(A)=2$

Product of roots $=|\mathrm{A}|=-3$

Let $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ c & d \end{array}\right ]$

We have $\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{d}=2$

$\mathrm{ad}-\mathrm{bc}=-3$

$A^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ c & d \end{array}\right ]\times \left [\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ c & d \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} a^{2}+bc & ab+bd \\ ac+cd & bc+d^{2} \end{array}\right ]$

We need $a^{2}+bc+bc+d^{2}$

$\begin{array}{l} =a^{2}+2bc+d^{2} \\ =(a+d)^{2}-2ad+2bc \\ =4-2(ad-bc) \\ =4-2(-3) \\ =4+6 \\ =10 \end{array}$

text: Let the complex numbers $α$ and $\frac{1}{\bar{α}}$ lie on the circles $|z-z_{0}|^{2}=4$ and $|z-z_{0}|^{2}=16$ respectively, where $z_{0}=1+i$. Then, the value of $100|α|^{2}$ is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} |z-z_{0}|^{2}=4 \\ \Rightarrow (α-z_{0})(\bar{α}-\bar{z}_{0})=4 \\ \Rightarrow α\bar{α}-α\bar{z}_{0}-z_{0}\bar{α}+|z_{0}|^{2}=4 \\ \Rightarrow |α|^{2}-α\bar{z}_{0}-z_{0}\bar{α}=2\text{......... (1)} \\ |z-z_{0}|^{2}=16 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \left (\dfrac{1}{\bar{α}}-z_{0}\right )\left (\dfrac{1}{α}-\bar{z}_{0}\right )=16 \\ \Rightarrow (1-\bar{α}z_{0})(1-α\bar{z}_{0})=16|α|^{2} \\ \Rightarrow 1-\bar{α}z_{0}-α\bar{z}_{0}+|α|^{2}|z_{0}|^{2}=16|α|^{2} \\ \Rightarrow 1-\bar{α}z_{0}-α\bar{z}_{0}=14|α|^{2}\text{....... (2)} \end{array}$

From (1) and (2)

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 5|α|^{2}=1 \\ \Rightarrow 100|α|^{2}=20 \end{array}$

text: If the solution curve, of the differential equation $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{x+y-2}{x-y}$ passing through the point $(2,1)$ is $\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{y-1}{x-1}\right )-\frac{1}{β}\log _{\mathrm{e}}\left (α+\left (\frac{y-1}{x-1}\right )^{2}\right )=\log _{\mathrm{e}}|x-1|$, then $5β+α$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left. \begin{array}{l} \dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{x+y-2}{x-y} \\ \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{X}+\mathrm{h},\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{Y}+\mathrm{k} \\ \dfrac{dY}{dX}=\dfrac{X+Y}{X-Y} \\ \begin{array}{l} \mathrm{h}+\mathrm{k}-2=0 \\ \mathrm{h}-\mathrm{k}=0 \end{array}\right \}\mathrm{h}=\mathrm{k}=1 \\ \mathrm{Y}=\mathrm{vX} \\ v+X\dfrac{dv}{dX}=\dfrac{1+v}{1-v}\Rightarrow X\dfrac{dv}{dX}=\dfrac{1+v^{2}}{1-v} \\  \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{1-v}{1+v^{2}}dv=\dfrac{dX}{X} \\ \tan ^{-1}v-\dfrac{1}{2}\ln \left (1+v^{2}\right )=\ln |X|+C \end{array}$

As curve is passing through $(2,1)$

$\begin{array}{l} \tan ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{y-1}{x-1}\right )-\dfrac{1}{2}\ln \left (1+\left (\dfrac{y-1}{x-1}\right )^{2}\right )=\ln |x-1| \\ \therefore α=1\text{and}β=2 \\ \Rightarrow 5β+α=11 \end{array}$
